sources.title: Valérie Gillet, Devotion and Dominion: Ninth-Century Donations of a Pandyan King in Temples along the River Kaveri (2017)
sources.note: Author-deposited publication abstract directly read, DOI 10.1163/15728536-06003002. Thirty inscriptions, Varaguna II identification, proposed reign beginning 862, thirteen-year Kaveri sovereignty from fourth regnal year. Grouped with author’s DHARMA reedition below.

sources.title: Valérie Gillet, Pandya inscription at Tiruccirrampalam, DHARMA INSPandya00014
sources.note: Direct edition and commentary read: middle text lost from repeated hand contact at sanctuary doorway, southern doorjamb, Varaguna fourth plus twelfth year. Same research as Gillet 2017; combined budget.

sources.title: K. V. Subrahmanya Aiyar, Tiruchchendur inscription of Varaguna-Maharaja II, Epigraphia Indica XXI
sources.note: Printed pages 102 to 104 directly read; page 103 scan downloaded and visually inspected, exact Tamil Latin transliteration and editor’s English rendering. Page viewer 131 = printed 102; 132 = printed 103. Ninth-century Vatteluttu Tamil record. Whole EI XXI counted as one work.

sources.title: A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar, South Indian Inscriptions XIV: The Pandyas, stone inscriptions 51 to 75
sources.note: Direct primary edition summaries, especially numbers 56, 59 and 62. Ambasamudram land improvement; Perungulam lamps and gong dedicated for mother and father. Rajasimha identification has chronological uncertainties, so public examples use broad early medieval dates.

sources.title: South Indian Inscriptions XIV, number 45: Sittannavasal
sources.note: Primary edition number 45/printed page 35, indexed original and ASI volume PDF. Teacher from Madurai repairs inner hall and builds front mandapa under Srivallabha. Grouped with other SII XIV source.

sources.title: Lisa N. Owen, Demarcating Sacred Space: The Jina Images at Kalugumalai (2010)
sources.note: Full scholarly PDF read. Printed pages 5, 10, 15: musicians, unfinished carving, female teachers and donors. Nine/early tenth-century dating is a scholarly attribution with broader dates in earlier literature.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Rock-cut Jain Cave Temple, Sittannavasal
sources.note: Official page accessed through indexed original text; direct fetch returned error. Ninth-century restoration, lotus pond, jumping fish, two painting layers exposed in cleaning. Earlier seventh-century cave attribution and aesthetic superiority claims omitted.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Department of Archaeology, Copper Plate Inscriptions
sources.note: Official indexed original text accessed; direct fetch error. Pandya seventh to tenth-century Vatteluttu Tamil and Grantha Sanskrit, ring-bound plates and chance discoveries. No claim that all documents use both languages or everyone was literate.

sources.title: E. Hultzsch, Udayendiram plates of Prithivipati II Hastimalla, South Indian Inscriptions II.76, DHARMA edition
sources.note: Direct edition, introduction and translation read. Verses 9 to 11 report Parantaka I taking Madurai and defeating Rajasimha and a Lankan army; verse 18 is Sripurambiyam battle. Fifteenth regnal year. Royal praise and opponent viewpoint explicit. Outdated introductory absolute Chola dates not used.

proposedOverrides.name: Pandya state
proposedOverrides.summary: Pandya kings, temple economies and communities in the ninth and tenth centuries.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct 800 to 1000 narrative; no aliases or replacement of pandyas 500 to 800 or pandya-state-1279 1279 to 1492.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Two identical imported outlines. Point-in-polygon omits Madurai and Sittannavasal, includes Kalugumalai, Tiruchendur and Ambasamudram. Serious incompleteness stated in public overview; Kaveri political reach lies beyond outline.
batchIdentityNotes.dating: No exact midpoint item years. Temple food and writing are ninth century, Kalugumalai generally ninth/early tenth by Owen, SII local donations early medieval with regnal chronology uncertainty. Earlier/later Pandya history remains distinct.
